mount.description: Mount the grid with all the rows (data already in memory). "Visible" = from setState to the end of the first frame committed with the whole viewport (first/last visible row and column) showing the right content. "Settled" = until the first frame committed after the grid's last DOM mutation. Memory is the JS heap retained by the grid after GC (heap after mount - heap before mount).

sort-string.description: Click the "code" column header (string column, unique-ish values) - first click sorts ascending (cold), second click descending. Measured from pointerdown to the end of the first frame committed with all visible rows sorted (and each row consistent: its cells belong to the same data row).

metrics.label: Ascending: click to sorted rows painted
Descending: click to sorted rows painted

sort-number.description: Click the "salary" column header (number column, unique-ish values) - first click sorts ascending (cold), second click descending. Measured from pointerdown to the end of the first frame committed with all visible rows sorted (and each row consistent: its cells belong to the same data row).

metrics.label: Ascending: click to sorted rows painted
Descending: click to sorted rows painted

scroll-jump.description: Programmatic jumps to 10 far-away scroll positions (like dragging the scrollbar thumb). Measured from setting scrollTop to the end of the first frame committed with the first and last visible rows showing the right content, at the right position.

metrics.label: Jump to rows painted (median of jumps)

scroll-vertical.description: Wheel-scroll down 24000px at 8000px/s (Input.synthesizeScrollGesture - real input pipeline, same gesture for every grid). Frame outcomes come from Chrome's compositor (PipelineReporter): "partial" = frame shown without the main thread's update, "dropped" = no new frame. rAF frame intervals and Long Animation Frames come from the page.

scroll-horizontal.description: Wheel-scroll right/left over all columns, 4 sweeps at 4000px/s (Input.synthesizeScrollGesture - real input pipeline, same gesture for every grid). Frame outcomes come from Chrome's compositor (PipelineReporter): "partial" = frame shown without the main thread's update, "dropped" = no new frame. rAF frame intervals and Long Animation Frames come from the page.

correctness-vertical.description: Same kind of vertical wheel gesture, faster (20000px/s). After every painted frame, samples points across the body and checks the cell there is the one that should be there for the current scroll position: "blank" = no cell, "wrong" = a cell for another row/column (stale content, or position lagging behind the scroll). This is the main thread's view of the frame; it reads layout, so it is never combined with the timing passes.

correctness-horizontal.description: Same kind of horizontal wheel gesture. After every painted frame, samples points across the body and checks the cell there is the one that should be there for the current scroll position: "blank" = no cell, "wrong" = a cell for another row/column (stale content, or position lagging behind the scroll). This is the main thread's view of the frame; it reads layout, so it is never combined with the timing passes.

visual-blank-vertical.description: Fast vertical wheel gesture (20000px/s) while recording what the compositor actually displays (CDP screencast). Each frame is checked for blank areas: vertical runs of the body with no text where rows should be. Unlike the correctness probe, this also catches the compositor scrolling ahead of the main thread. Screencast capture skips frames under load and adds overhead - compare the grids, not absolute numbers.
